review.summary: ManY participates directly in PEP-dependent sugar group translocation.
review.reason: ManY performs substrate binding and membrane translocation in ManXYZ. The resolved three-subunit study establishes coupled transport/phosphorylation. This is core pathway work, not a generic inference from growth or mere coexpression.

supported_by.supporting_text: All three subunits are required for sugar transport and phosphorylation

review.summary: Erni et al. (1987) directly demonstrated that ManY is part of the mannose PTS permease, which mediates sugar transport with concomitant phosphorylation. All three subunits are required for sugar transport and phosphorylation. This annotation was made by ComplexPortal based on PMID:2951378.
review.reason: Strong experimental evidence directly establishing ManY as a component of the PTS. This is a core function annotation.

supported_by.supporting_text: The mannose permease of the bacterial phosphotransferase system mediates sugar transport across the cytoplasmic membrane concomitant with sugar phosphorylation...All three subunits are required for sugar transport and phosphorylation
